A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EVM-QuestBench research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 20 models, including benchmark scores, execution diagnostics, and task-level failure analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original five-round evaluations of 20 models and a validator-tolerance analysis covering 10,700 task instances.

M1.justification: The JSON task specifications, dynamic parameter sampling, TypeScript interface, composite planning procedure, weighted atomic validation, and step-efficiency scoring remain unchanged. The new walkthrough documents the existing pipeline rather than establishing an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 107 BSC tasks: 62 atomic and 45 composite, with the same transaction, DeFi, query, and advanced-operation coverage. Expanded breakdowns and case studies do not establish additional tasks or domains.

E2.justification: The main 20-model roster is retained after matching aliases. However, Table 2 expands the composite diagnostic comparison from 13 to 20 models, adding entries such as Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and GPT-5.1. The overhead comparison expands from nine models in v1 Table 9 to seventeen in v2 Table 11.

E3.justification: Table 10 changes reported composite coverage for Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3-Coder-30B, and Devstral-2512 from 0/45 to 45/45. Table 2 removes first-try and ethers-error-rate metrics. New Appendix D.3 introduces re-scoring with tolerance multipliers from 0.5× to 3×; the main execution settings and scoring rules remain stable.

E4.justification: V2 adds a benchmark-wide tolerance-sensitivity analysis and deviation breakdown in Appendix D.3/Table 8. It retains v1's two cases under H.1–H.2 and adds cases covering numerical misinterpretation, planning failure, and partial execution. Difficulty and overhead analyses are expanded, while quantitative first-try and ethers-error analyses are removed.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports only one run per model and cannot estimate uncertainty. V2 explicitly increases this to five independent rounds, reporting means, standard deviations, coefficients of variation, t-based 95% confidence intervals, and inter-round Spearman correlations with significance information in Section 5.1 and Table 1.

E6.justification: Scores and rankings are extensively replaced by five-round estimates. Table 1 changes from Gemini-3-Pro leading with 8,217 to Claude-Sonnet-4.5 leading with an 8,236 mean; Gemini-3-Pro's mean is 7,863. Retained case pass rates change from 45% to 59% and 40% to 56%. New tolerance results report invariant scores and rankings. Different repetition protocols preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions, planning objective, atomic scoring equation, and composite decay formula are retained. V2's standard confidence-interval formula documents statistical estimation without adding a theoretical result or revising the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the modular execution-grounded benchmark, atomic/composite separation, standardized execution protocol, and observed capability asymmetry. Five-round reporting strengthens the evidence supporting these retained claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: V2 introduces an interpretation of tolerance invariance based on essentially exact-or-failed outputs. It replaces v1's treatment of early-terminated models as excluded coverage artifacts with discussion of measured interface failures. Section 7 replaces the single-run limitation with qualifications about overlapping confidence intervals and adds configurable fork-pinning guidance; new cases explain additional failure mechanisms.

D1.justification: New Appendix G details percentage-transfer generation, execution, validator weights, and task-specific amount and balance tolerances. Section 7 newly discloses configuration-based fork pinning, without establishing its use in the reported evaluations. Dependencies, runner interfaces, and the policy of withholding full outputs and traces remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 16 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Bibliography ordering, citation formatting, and added reference URLs are presentation changes.

P1.justification: Results and limitations receive localized rewrites, names are standardized, and the appendices gain a walkthrough and additional case subsections. Most methodological exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a single-column report with branded headers and a boxed abstract. V1 Figure 2 is split into v2 Figures 2–3; several plots are redesigned, a ranking chart and deviation table are added, and diagnostic table columns and figure placements are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses v1's explicit single-run weakness through repeated evaluations, uncertainty estimates, and ranking-stability checks, while adding benchmark-wide validator-sensitivity evidence. Internal score consistency also improves: GPT-5's composite scores conflict between v1 Tables 1–2 (2,443 versus 3,962), whereas both v2 tables report 3,646. These substantial reliability gains outweigh the removed first-try/ethers diagnostics and a limited reporting error: Section 5.1 claims 15 models have CV below 9%, while Table 1 shows 14.
